Hi Jared — thanks for the clear ask. Short answer up front: we charge for input + output tokens, and we apply two billing layers for long-window workloads: (1) per-request rounding to a billing grain, and (2) optional context-bucketing for large aggregated workloads to avoid extremely high per-request spikes on negotiated Dedicated plans. Details and examples below.

Quick bullets:
- Standard hosted API: we sum input + output tokens and round up to the nearest 32-token increment for billing. There is also a platform minimum of 16 billed tokens per request.
- Long-window / archival SKU: for single requests > 8k tokens we switch to the "context-bucket" model: requests are allocated into 1,024-token buckets for billing. That means a 60k-token input is accounted as 60k / 1,024 = 58.6 -> billed as 59 buckets * bucket_price. Output tokens are still billed per 32-token rounding.
- Dedicated & committed customers: we can negotiate smaller bucket sizes (e.g., 512 tokens) and tighter rounding granularity as part of an SLO/commit.
- Streaming: low-latency streaming calls (where you keep an open connection and send incremental tokens) are billed per 32-token round as tokens arrive; the 16-token minimum still applies per logical request (end of stream).

Examples (hosted API default):
1) Short session: input 180 tokens + output 220 tokens = 400 total -> round up to nearest 32 -> 416 billed tokens (since 400 -> next 32 increment is 416).
2) Mid-length: input 4,000 + output 1,000 = 5,000 -> round up to 5,024 billed tokens.
3) Archival single request (60,000 input, 3,000 output): input buckets = ceil(60000 / 1024) = 59 buckets. Input billed = 59 * bucket_size_equivalent (we convert bucket to token-equivalent for accounting) -> 59 * 1024 = 60,416 token-equivalent billed for input. Output 3,000 -> round to 3,008. Total billed tokens = 60,416 + 3,008 = 63,424.

Note: the bucket-to-token conversion above is to keep unit economics comparable in dashboards; customers on Dedicated may instead receive a flat per-bucket price (e.g., negotiated bucket price) which can be cheaper than token-equivalent pricing.

I'll loop in Karthik for nuances around streaming and caching, and Monica will attach a sample spreadsheet with these calculations for procurement.

Hi all — a couple of technical clarifications from infra side that affect billed tokens: 

- Caching: when prefix/KV caching serves repeated context chunks we do not re-bill cached tokens for that request; instead we bill only the tokens that were materialized (delta). For billing reports we show both raw token consumption and effective billed tokens after cache credits.
- KV/chunking for archival: if you chunk a 60k doc into N smaller calls (e.g., 12x 5k inputs) those will each be bucketed separately under hosted defaults; however, on a Dedicated contract we can enable aggregate billing where we sum raw tokens for a batch job and apply bucketing on the aggregate (reduces rounding overhead).
- Streaming interim charges: partial streaming frames are not billed until the request completes (end-of-stream marker). This avoids micro-billing for each small frame.

If you want, Monica and I can run a model of your weekly profiles and show expected billed tokens/month under (A) hosted defaults, (B) Dedicated with 512 buckets, (C) Dedicated with aggregated batch billing.

-karthik
Senior Product Manager, Redwood Inference

Preliminary commercial range (for discussion only) would be $0.0025 - $0.0035 per 512-bucket depending on commit level and whether you want aggregated monthly true-up. Monica will propose two firm numbers in the pricing appendix.

3) One-off credit: happy to propose a $5k first-month rounding credit as part of the SOW for pilots > $50k ARR commitment. We can make that conditional in the draft SOW.
